correctness.rationale: The pure adjacency/equality classification is correct. In the finite recurrence, fixed-depth exact set interning (including repeated picks) is equivalent to both directions of the next-move condition; the terminal labels distinguish equality, adjacency and neither. I independently computed all ordered vertex choices with masks for the fourth-point profiles, without orbit reduction: widths 3–8 give twelve distinct types, and both twists at every width 9–32 give one distinct common type. For the unbounded range, a short signed cyclic gap of matching length has a mod-two constraint on its two endpoint offsets. Splitting at equal positions gives consistent new constraints because transport parities add, even when the old gap goes once around from a sole selected column to itself. In a long gap, at most one subgap is below the next cutoff; match that subgap and its parity, or leave both new gaps above the cutoff. Repeated columns respect the offset, including rungs and repeated vertices. Terminal length-one gaps preserve all horizontal adjacency. This proves the unbounded bridge through width 32 and the sharp within-family 18-vertex bound. At width nine the ordinary prism is planar and the twisted ladder nonplanar. The PASS is for the stated pure-language finding; the blanket scope remark about adding column/rung predicates should instead specify an expansion or say richer signatures are not addressed.
residual_risks: Finite replay does not prove the gap lemma; it was checked separately. No claim for richer languages or higher ranks.
